claim: Athletic loco-manipulation policies for a quadruped+arm system (19 DoF) are trained using Isaac Sim with 4096 parallel environments using PPO (RSL-RL), but total step counts and wall-clock training times are not reported in the paper.
stance_target: Training budget for quadruped loco-manipulation RL
scope_conditions: Unitree B2 quadruped + Z1 Pro arm; Isaac Sim; MIT Supercloud HPC cluster
quoted_support: we designed the training environment in Isaac Sim with 4096 parallel environments. We train policies with the RSL-RL implementation of PPO with default hyperparameters

claim: A two-stage WBC pre-training + task-specific RL fine-tuning pipeline substantially outperforms both training from scratch and a frozen-WBC high-level policy approach for athletic loco-manipulation.
stance_target: Pre-train then fine-tune is the dominant paradigm for complex legged robot learning
scope_conditions: Athletic tasks: throwing, lifting, sled-pulling; quadruped manipulator platform
quoted_support: End-to-end fine-tuning from a pre-trained WBC leads to the best task performance.

claim: A single pre-trained WBC can serve as initialization for multiple task-specific fine-tuning runs (throw, lift, sled-pull), avoiding repeated pre-training and reducing total compute.
stance_target: Shared pre-training amortizes compute cost across multiple task fine-tunes
scope_conditions: Three athletic tasks tested; quadruped manipulator; Isaac Sim PPO training
quoted_support: The same WBC base policy weights can be reused for multiple task policies, thus avoiding repeated pre-training.

claim: The Unsupervised Actuator Net (UAN) is trained from approximately 5 minutes of real hardware data using RL to predict corrective torques, providing a data-efficient alternative to torque-sensor-based actuator networks.
stance_target: Actuator calibration via small real-world datasets enables effective sim-to-real transfer
scope_conditions: Unitree Z1 Pro arm with harmonic drive actuators; no torque sensors; RL-based UAN training
quoted_support: We collect data on the real hardware to construct a dataset of transitions... for about 5 minutes.

claim: Reward hacking in task-reward-only training can be mitigated by accurate actuator modeling (UAN) rather than penalty enumeration, since the policy cannot exploit simulator imperfections that no longer exist.
stance_target: Accurate simulation reduces reward hacking better than adding more penalty terms
scope_conditions: Athletic whole-body loco-manipulation; task-only reward (no dense tracking); quadruped+arm
quoted_support: UAN mitigates reward hacking by ensuring that the learned behaviors remain robust and transferable.
